#4384. Valkyrie Connect tier list - Best PVE and PVP characters

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version: 10.28.0

If you are eager to check out a complete Valkyrie Connect tier list of all the best characters, then you're in the right place. Today, we are going to delve into it and list all heroes based on their strengths, so you will always know which ones to prioritise upgrading.

In Valkyrie Connect there are hundreds of characters, and if you really want to min-max all the content, then you will need to adapt your picks based on the type of enemy (or enemies) you are facing. It would be impossible to offer a list that is valid for everyone since chances are no two players will have the exact same heroes at their disposal. Therefore, take this information with a grain of salt, and don't despair if you don't have the top characters sitting in the S+ tier. You can always use the characters that match your requirements and are next in line, they will do just fine.

Before you go through the list, note that we have a vast collection of similar articles that include a Battle Cats tier list, T3 Arena tier list, Darkest Dungeon tier list, and a lot of others.  Valkyrie Connect's best characters  Let's make one thing clear - there is not one single character (or even a couple of characters) that could be considered universally 'the best'. There are many heroes that do well in PvE and several that are exceptional in PvP. If you want to clear both, then most of the time you need to upgrade multiple characters. That will take time and is by no means anyone just starting out with only a handful of Valkyries.

Of course, some of the characters (such as Vindicator Gratias) can be SSS tier in both Story Mode and Arena, so you should upgrade those first. But if you don't have them, then you can always make two different parties and use them for whichever content you prefer.

To give you a hand, we've divided the tier list into two, one for PvE and one for PvP. If you're interested in a particular hero, you can search for them by name and you will most definitely find it listed somewhere. If you cannot find the hero you've been looking for, then it probably was not released (yet) or is not in the Global version of the game, which is what this Valkyrie Connect tier list is for.

So without further ado, let's dive right into it!

#4383. Top War tier list - Every hero ranked

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version: 1.683.0

In Top War, there are quite a lot of things that you could consider 'farmable', and in certain situations, heroes might be considered one of these things. And since there are just so many heroes out there, it could be quite difficult to choose a handful and make them your number one priority.

Don't despair though, below we've compiled a Top War tier list of all the best heroes in the game so you can choose the best ones according to your needs. The heroes can provide specific buffs and their kit can be extremely good in certain situations, but if you really want some additional info about these heroes, I've got you covered.

Most of the heroes on the Top War tier list are SSR Before we take a look at the Top War tier list though, I'll start by mentioning that the rarity of the heroes (SSR, SR, and R) plays a very important role in the game. The higher a hero's rarity, the more troops can join them in battle (SSR heroes can take a lot more troops than R heroes).

Therefore, it shouldn't come as a surprise that all the top-tier heroes are SSR. If you want to get SSR heroes too, all you need to do is keep playing the game - even as a f2p player you are bound to get a few eventually!

All the heroes have a type - some of them are Air Force heroes, some are Army heroes, and others are Navy Heroes. In the tier list, you will find them all divided by their type, so it will be a lot easier for you to pick the best ones based on what they should specialize in.

If you want to learn more about the game, make sure you check out our other Top War articles!

Maximo - A powerful hero that will greatly enhance any air force units and can quite literally change the entire course of a battle. He's a premium hero who is worth investing in, and by all means, one who can work on the offensive and defensive front.

Selina - She's a good hero thanks to the amazing buffs she provides, and if you manage to max her out, she greatly increases the maximum HP of other units, as well as their attack. Serval - Another broken premium hero that can make life a living hell for enemies. She's especially good when paired up with some of the other top-tier heroes, since they can stack their stats.

Preycis - This Army hero is great for aiming at the back-row enemies and is one of the best at specialising in that. He doesn't have a whole lot of other buffs (when compared to other heroes), but the sheer amount of damage dealt to the back row cannot go unnoticed. Shinji Ikari - A highly versatile hero, he can be obtained for a limited time only, but during that time, it's crucial to get him. He can be used for pretty much any type of content and has an ability that grants indestructibility for two rounds, which is definitely worth it. Optimus Prime - Another collab character that is impossible to overlook is Optimus Prime, the best Transformer out there (correct?). He can also grant an indestructibility buff, and when maxed out, is absolutely top-tier.

#4382. After Cancelling Zelda Switch 2 Pre-Orders, Walmart Is Now Supposedly Sending Out $519 Gift Cards

Some customers also claim they've been able to "reorder" the system

Last week, Walmart reportedly cancelled Zelda Switch 2 pre-orders a day before the launch after it "oversold" the consoles.

In an update, the retailer is apparently giving out vouchers in response to the upset these cancellations have caused. As highlighted by Polygon, some customers are now supposedly being compensated with "$519 gift cards".

Here's the email response customers are now receiving from Walmart (confirmed by deal website CheapAssGamer.com):

We know you were looking forward to your preorder of Nintendo Switch 2 Legend of Zelda, and we sincerely apologize that we canceled your pre-order. This was our mistake.

To show our appreciation for you as a Walmart customer and help make up for the canceled order, we're sending you a Walmart eGift Card for $519.99. You'll receive this gift card via email within 10 business days.

Again, we're sorry for the mistake. Thank you for being a Walmart customer. We look forward to serving you again soon.

According to the same story, these customers are also being given the chance to reorder the Zelda-themed Switch 2, and the gift card "essentially grants what sounds like a free Switch 2".

Based on some other customer stories online, Walmart may also be offering "one or the other", where the customer gets to either reorder the limited edition system or can get a gift card matching the cost of this unit.

There's also speculation that this offer from Walmart is "too good to be true" and could potentially be another blunder. However, multiple customers have noted how it's come from the '[email protected]' email address, so it seems promising.

#4381. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4380. The fastest cars in CSR Racing 2, in every tier

Updated with the very best cars to race in 2026

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version: 6.7.2

Want to quickly compare stats on all the cars in CSR Racing 2? Then this is the guide for you.

Below, we've listed all the base stats for every car and highlighted which wins in each category. R stands for Rep Bonus, and F is for Fusion Slots.

Obviously, every car can be completely changed through upgrades and tuning, but these starting numbers give you a good indication of that car's overall abilities. It provides a quick glimpse at the stats, which might just be enough to help you pick out which car to choose to purchase next.

We've also included some thoughts on which are the best cars in CSR Racing 2 - both rare imports and those you can buy with in-game cash.

Just click through below to find out the fastest cars in every tier.

Many great choices in this category. At first glance, it seems like the Golf GTI MK1 is a clear winner, especially as it also has a 6% RP bonus and eight fusion slots. However, it must be won in the Rare Imports lot, which means it's a lot harder to come by.

On top of that, the fastest car so far is the Ford Mustang Boss 302 with e.c level 50, which means, even though it's not as fast early on, it can make it up in the later stages.

The Veloster Turbo R Spec is also a decent choice, but can only be purchased with (150) Gold.

The M235i Coupe is a fantastic car for Tier 2, especially since you can buy it for just $75,000. It's light and has high power, but you'll need to upgrade your tyres to bring the grip up.

Potentially, the Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Coupe can be the fastest in this tier and by quite a big margin. Not early on, though. The same goes for the Ferrari 250 GTO and Aston Martin DB5.

If you want Tier 2's best vehicle, you'll need to earn the F-150 from the Rare Imports lot.

The Ferrari California 30 is obviously still one of the best Tier 3 cars in class - no wonder it's being kept back as a prize.

So if you can't win that, the SRT Hellcat at 825 G is a good choice with its high power, low shift time, and strong grip. If you only have dollars to spend, get the RS 5 Coupe.

At level 50, the Pontiac GTO "The Judge" is the fastest car in this category. The BMW M2 (G87) Coupe "M Performance" is right behind it in second place. As you would expect, any variant of the Civic Type R is going to be fast! This is one of my favourite categories, as there are several good choices.

The GT-R (R35) Premium looks like a pretty good vehicle for this tier. Not only is it affordable, but it has an amazing grip (too much, perhaps?!) and a low shift time. You'll need to work on power and lowering the weight with a lighter body.

The Viper ACR is another good option: it has great power for the tier, a low shift time, and 23 Fusion Slots.

Right now, the Rocket Bunny is looking more attractive than ever, but the big Grand Cherokee Trackhawk is tempting too.

At this point, the game has some amazing cars to use, and the latest releases push performance to the limits. These are by far the fastest cars in CSR Racing 2. The Bugatti Chiron is a fantastic choice, as is the FXX K, but launch cars such as the Bugatti Veyron and One:1 are still great.

If you don't want to rely on Rare Import lot wins, the Aventador LP 700-4 is a good bet with its high power, strong grip, and its relatively lightweight to boot.

Regardless, though, there's no doubt you'll have fun with vehicles like the 'Cuda "TorC" in CSR2.

#4379. 10 Soulslikes Where You’re Actually the Villain

Shane is a Contributor for DualShockers writing guides and other materials. He has a degree in Game Design and Criticism.

​Of all the genres in gaming, there isn’t one that stays as morally ambiguous as soulslikes. While the genre has grown to encompass a lot of different kinds of games, that question of morality remains the same.

Players are often a bit hesitant to become the villain of the story, but offering up that potential makes for a more difficult choice. Whether a player will embrace evil or remain on the path of good always makes for a good time.

This list consists of games that could be categorized as soulslike even if their main genre is a bit different. It does contain spoilers for certain endings, so you may want to read carefully to avoid anything you’d rather not know.

If you're ready to root for the bad guy, then check out this list of shooters where you're actually the villain!

Hellpoint is an interesting soulslike game that sees players take on the role of a Spawn as they face off against all kinds of cosmic horrors. While trapped on a space station, players will make their way through boss encounters while making choices to determine their alignment.

You don’t have to play as the villain in Hellpoint, but you do have the option to align yourself with the Prodigal Spawn and perform a dark ritual. It is morally grey, but those choices do matter and can make players into the villain of their story.

In a genre that typically sticks to being morally grey, Death’s Gambit: Afterlife makes things a bit harder by making you an agent of death. In this Metroidvania soulslike, players will go up against immortals as they attempt to snuff out immortality altogether.

This one is tough because your motivations aren’t necessarily evil, but the results you achieve certainly make you a bit of a villain. By destroying immortality, you’ll be killing anything and everything connected to it, regardless of alignment.

You wouldn't typically imagine a game about giant robots digging so deep into the ambiguity of who a mercenary decides to fight for, but Armored Core VI does just that. The game is more of an action game than a soulslike, but with FromSoftware at the wheel, it still feels like one.

Playing as C4-621, you have a choice in who you help, and depending on your choice, a lot of things can happen. Despite the choice of endings, you do spend a lot of time fighting and killing the residents of Rubicon 3.

If you're tired of being the good guy, then check out this list of JRPGs where you play as the anti-hero!

FromSoftware really enjoys giving players a choice in how they affect the world as a whole, and most of the time it's not for the better. Playing as an Ashen One, players will have to face off against the mighty Lords of Cinder and decide the fate of the world.

There is still that freedom of choice, but players can choose to simply burn the world themselves. This certainly makes you a villain to some, but it is still a choice, so it’s up to players if they become a villain.

As a Hunter in Bloodborne, your only purpose is to kill the monsters that plague the world and use their power to make yourself stronger. You may not start very villainous, but in the end you may become the very thing you set out to destroy.

In one of the endings, players can turn into a Great One, an otherworldly eldritch being that doesn’t follow our sense of morality. It could be up for debate whether this makes players the true villain, but it does seem a bit villainous to leave behind your humanity.

Elden Ring was a sensational game that expanded the soulslike genre into the open-world genre and gave players more freedom than ever before. With that freedom came plenty of choice, and those choices could end in disaster.

By taking the Frenzied Flame, players will cause a chain reaction of events that ends the game with the world on fire. The world may be a bit problematic, but causing mass destruction and burning the world to a crisp seems very villainous.

While playing as the protagonist, Wolf, players are given choices, some of which have long-standing consequences. The game isn’t a traditional soulslike, but with the difficulty and mechanics behind the game, it certainly feels like one.

Wolf is given a choice towards the back half of the game where he can either follow Iron Code or save Kuro. Following the code results in Wolf fully becoming a demon and killing many of the people he knows and cares about.

With interesting characterization and backstories, these are the JRPGs Where the Villain Feels More Compelling Than the Hero.

The premise of the game seems to frame your character as the hero, but in true FromSoftware fashion, you can become the villain. Featuring a morality tracker, the more you kill innocents and do vile deeds, the closer you become to being Pure Black.

At the end of the game, players can decide to simply betray their allies up to that point, killing them and thrusting the world into a new age of darkness. Whether you were the villain throughout the game or not, at the end there’s no debating it.

Vampires are pretty much always the bad guys, although when it comes to Dr. Jonathan Reid, players can decide what happens. Whether he succumbs to the monster within or maintains some semblance of humanity is in the hands of players.

Whatever path the player takes determines what happens to London and its people. Leaning into the destructive nature of vampires leaves the city in complete collapse and causes the epidemic to continue unfettered.

Final Fantasy games as a whole have always been a bit out there in terms of story, but unlike the other games on this list, you are literally the villain. Playing as Jack along with the other Strangers as you attempt to stop Chaos from destroying the world.

By the end of the story, there’s only one option for our heroes, and that’s for Jack to embrace the Chaos and become the villain of the story. This sends him back in time and sets him up as Garland, the villain of the first Final Fantasy game.

If you're bad to the bone, then check out these 8 Games Where Evil Is The Only Option.

Yakuza/Like a Dragon developer Ryu Ga Gotoku Studios is releasing its quasi-prequel game, Stranger Than Heaven, in January, and ahead of its release, the team has been pulling back the curtain on protagonist Makoto Daito's decades-spanning adventure through Japan. #4377. CD Projekt Red Poaches Another Warhorse Lead

Melissa Sarnowski is a Gaming Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in lists, reviews, and features, with additional experience writing guides for Hardcore Gamer. Before joining DualShockers, Melissa contributed to Screen Rant, and she currently writes for CBR and

CD Projekt Red continues to add talented developers to its team, particularly those who were working in lead roles at Warhorse Studios, as noticed by b0ysbrokenheart on X (formerly Twitter). The latest addition is Zbynek Zelinka, whom b0ysbrokenheart showed using a screenshot of Zelinka's LinkedIn profile showing his current job as a Senior Gameplay Designer at CD Projekt Red, starting in October 2026.

In an recent interview, it was discussed how The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt devs were initially told they could not make it.

Zelinka was previously a Lead Technical Designer at Warhorse Studios, where he worked for a total of seven years and 10 months, rising from Technical Designer to Senior Technical Designer and eventually Lead Technical Designer before departing for CD Projekt Red.

In addition to Zelinka, Zdenek Glatz and Karel Kolmann have also left Warhorse Studios for CD Projekt Red in the last year. All three of these developers were at Warhorse Studios for seven or eight years, meaning CD Projekt Red is picking up some highly experienced employees, at least two of whom have been involved in the development of both Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2.

Glatz joined CD Projekt Red in May 2026, according to his LinkedIn, as a Senior Open World Designer. Before that, he was a Lead Level Designer at Warhorse Studios, having previously worked as a Game Designer/Writer and Senior Game Designer/Writer at the studio. He's bringing eight and a half years of experience to CD Projekt Red with him.

In addition to Zelinka, Zdenek Glatz and Karel Kolmann have also left Warhorse Studios for CD Projekt Red in the last year.

Kolmann joined CD Projekt Red in November 2025 as a Senior Quest Designer. She spent just over eight years at Warhorse Studios before that, starting as a Writer and Game Designer in 2017, then moving to Senior Game Designer and eventually to Lead Gameplay Designer. With them together, CD Projekt Red gains a combined 24 years of game design experience to add to their in-progress projects.

CD Projekt Red has a few highly anticipated games in the works, and the company is clearly doing its best to grab talented developers to help bring those games to life. We know that CD Projekt Red is working on a sequel to Cyberpunk 2077, which has the placeholder name of Project Orion, and a job listing shows that they aren't finished searching for developers to help with the game.

Then, you have The Witcher 4 in development from CD Projekt Red, which continues the series by putting Ciri in the role of main character, and this project would be particularly fitting for the devs who left Warhorse Studios to work on it. The world of The Witcher has more magic and fantasy elements, but the general setting isn't that different from Kingdom Come: Deliverance. If I had to guess, I'd bet that the Witcher series is where the former Warhorse devs are going to be working.

They could also be put on The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion's development team, but the release date for that is close enough that I imagine a lot of the development is finished, and it's in the final stages, which leaves The Witcher 4 as the most likely choice, or the secretive Project Hadar new IP that we don't really know anything about.

Meanwhile, Warhorse Studios has another Kingdom Come game in the works and a Lord of the Rings game, but the comments on b0ysbrokenheart's X post show that people are a bit worried about these games as devs are leaving the studio for CD Projekt Red. One even asked CD Projekt Red to "hold their horses" for the sake of the next Kingdom Come game so it can be as good as the first two.

I'm not very worried about the projects, as all the studio closures mean that there are, unfortunately, a ton of talented developers currently out of work, and I'm sure many of them would be a great fit to join Warhorse Studios.

#4376. Round Up: The Reviews Are In For Stellar Blade's Switch 2 Port

It's all about Link this week, but there is another notable release arriving for the Switch 2 on the same day. It's Shift Up's action game, Stellar Blade.

We've already taken a look at the port here on Nintendo Life, and despite some drawbacks, Eve's outing stands tall on the hybrid platform. Here's how we summed it up:

"Despite some drawbacks, Stellar Blade stands tall as an impressive and enjoyable action game that occupies a nice niche in the Switch 2 library. Rewarding exploration, thrilling combat, and tough but fair difficulty carry this game far and make it an easy recommendation, even if its story can be a bit bland and the visuals aren’t always up to the task."

Review Stellar Blade: Complete Edition (Switch 2) - Perfectly Playable, Despite Drawbacks

So, what did other critics have to say? Read on to find out...

"Stellar Blade is one of the best action adventure titles to release in the current console generation. Comparisons to NieR: Automata and Bayonetta are inevitable (particularly with the DLC costumes to highlight the similarities), but mostly only down to shared aesthetics and some thematic similarities with the former, as the game carves out its own unique identity with its superb combat. The visual cuts are there, and it is absolutely unplayable with frame generation enabled, but with some slight tweaks to the default settings, it delivers a fantastic experience on Nintendo Switch 2 – particularly in handheld mode."

"Stellar Blade Complete Edition is a shining testament to what developers with the right know-how can achieve on Switch 2. Shift Up has clearly taken this project very seriously and they’re out to not only expand the reach of their IP, but also flaunt their technical chops. Having poured a ton of time into Stellar Blade Complete Edition"

"All told, Stellar Blade Complete Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 is a great way to experience Shift Up’s action game ahead of the series’ next entry. It might have some graphical blemishes on Nintendo’s comparatively underpowered hardware, but those blemishes don’t quite matter during the moment-to-moment, adrenaline-pumping gameplay that Stellar Blade delivers in spades."

"The Switch 2 version of Stellar Blade is competent but struggles to hit the same heights as the original. With its steady framerate, the game runs extremely well both docked and handheld. While it’s incredible that Shift Up has managed to get the game working on Nintendo’s latest hardware, some compromises have been made. Animations dip at a distance and the game isn’t as responsive as the original. It may not be the best version of the game, but it remains a worthwhile option for those who want to experience EVE’s adventure on the go."

"If you haven’t played this Korean hit, or want it on Nintendo consoles, now is the perfect opportunity. It includes Nier Automata and Goddess of Victory: Nikke DLCs, updates, and quality-of-life improvements. Properly optimized for Nintendo Switch 2, this port is an example of what developers can do when they set their minds to it. The exclusive Bayonetta DLC costumes are the icing on this cake. It does not apologize for being sexy and wears it with pride and honor. A game for fans and the consumer’s joy and awe. An example of what games can and should strive for."

#4375. Vampire Survivors tier list - Ranking characters from base game and DLCs

Each DLC brought different characters and we have decided to rank each one and rank them on the Vampire Survivors tier list according to their late-game power.

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version: 1.16.111

Since the release of Vampire Survivors, people have been widely discussing things like "Who are the best characters in the game?" and other burning questions. There are, god knows, how many characters at the moment, but even then, this list can still expand with every update. Picking the most powerful character is essential to enjoying Vampire Survivors, and we are here to help with that.

Potent characters will mean an easier time, so if you're not looking for a challenge, they're the way to go. If you're playing with any of them, you can kill enemies much more effectively and win even if you are a beginner. Below are the best characters in Vampire Survivors. Also, feel free to check our Dead Cells weapons tier list as well as this tier list for Capybara Go.

About Queen Sigma Even though Queen Sigma can't pick up Golden Eggs like other heroes, she is still one of the most powerful characters, and it wouldn't be wrong to call her the best character without a doubt.

She uses the Victory Sword, which is one of the game’s most potent weapons. After levelling up, she gets +1% Might and +1% Growth, allowing her to become much more powerful. The main feature of Queen Sigma is her 333 max health, allowing her to survive longer.

About Red Death Red Death is the fastest and scariest hero in Vampire Survivors. The high speed makes this character suitable for finding Relic locations and fighting hidden bosses. Red Death uses the Death Spiral that can be easily combined with Axe in the same run. Its main feature is the 20% Might increase and the 100% Movement increase. These stats make Red Death one of the most potent heroes in Vampire Survivors.

Pungola is a mighty Vampire Survivors character that has two primary weapons: Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow. The hero gets +1% Might every level and can be unlocked by opening a special coffin in Mad Forest. Also, you should cast the spell “flymetothemoon” in Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane to unlock this hero.

Ambrojoe is an easily attainable hero that uses La Robba as a primary weapon. This character has average stats and no special abilities, making him the best option for beginners. We have to note that the weapon looks an awful lot like a Kinder Egg - we're actually not sure if it's an easter egg or not.

Dommario can be a good option for beginners due to his powerful defence and attack stats, but the main disadvantage of Dommario is speed. It is one of the slowest characters you can choose.

Megalo Menya Moonspell is overall the best character in Legacy of Moonspell DLC due to her combination of survivability and damage.

What stands out particularly is her invincibility, meaning she cannot take damage at all during certain periods. That said, this comes with a limitation; she will disappear when the current time limit expires. This makes her particularly powerful for clearing stages quickly.

Je-Ne-Viv is considered the most powerful character in Tides of the Foscari DLC, and that's why she's at the top of this part of our Vampire Survivors tier list. She has a unique weapon called Insatiable, which scales with Magnet and Greed stats, and comes with the Shadow Servant. Her abilities deal significant area-of-effect damage, making her a powerful character overall.

Crewmate Dino gains permanent stat boosts whenever any player's weapon reaches its max level. This ability makes him especially powerful in co-op mode, making him the best character in the Emergency Meeting DLC.

Megalo Impostor Rina has high base stats, special weapon mechanics, and the ability to scale through all phases of the game. Her toolkit is ideal for those who enjoy a playstyle that rewards aggressive tactics and strategic planning.

About Colonel Bahamut Colonel Bahamut stands out because of his great passive bonuses, like +100 Max Health and +50% Might. His weapon, Metal Claw, allows for significant area damage, making him the best character in Operation Guns DLC, capable of scaling effectively with Greed and Curse mechanics.

About Alucard Alucard is S-Tier and one of the best characters in the Ode to Castlevania DLC due to his high damage output, versatility, and healing abilities. His weapon mechanics allow for powerful area control, making him a top-tier choice for most runs.

Sonia Belmont is the other top-tier character in Ode to Castlevania. She has excellent scaling potential and powerful weapon synergies. Her ability to deal consistent dps while maintaining survivability is what makes her so good.

About Vlad Tepes Dracula Vlad Tepes Dracula has a deserving top position on this Vampire Survivors tier list since he is a character with high damage output and abilities that enhance survivability. His skills allow him to deal significant area damage, making him a standout choice for many players.

About Lisa Tepes Lisa Tepes provides excellent support with healing abilities and buffs that can sustain her and allies throughout runs. Her versatility and ability to boost stats make her invaluable in longer gameplay sessions. About Cornell Cornell has strong offensive capabilities with transformation mechanics that allow him to adapt to different combat scenarios effectively. His versatility makes him a solid choice for various builds.

About Cosmo Even though Cosmo looks cute, he is one of the deadliest heroes in Vampire Survivors. The main feature of this character is that he does not have a primary weapon. So, you have more customisation options using Cosmo compared to other heroes. About Leda The primary weapon for Leda is the Holy Land, the improved version of the Magic Wand. She can equip both weapons to reach the highest effectiveness in the same run. Leda also has Passive Bonuses, which you can find below:

Gyorunton is another dragon in Tier S. It uses the Bracelet to kill enemies and has a special ability - Gyorunton can evolve weapons much faster than other heroes using Treasure Chest. Also, this hero has 300 Max Health, which is exceptionally high compared to the classic 100 Health Points.

About Smith IV Smith IV is a scary character who uses Vandalier as a primary weapon. This hero has +100% Luck and gets +1% Luck at every level, which is a unique ability. And for such a decisive boost, Smith IV pays with his stats.

About Gain Boros Gains Boros is a mighty dragon that uses Heaven Sword as the primary weapon. This character gains +2% Growth every time you level it up, making Heaven Sword more powerful.

And that’s our complete Vampire Survivors tier list. As you can see, the game has a significant diversity of exciting characters, and 3 of the best heroes in Vampire Survivors are Queen Sigma, Red Death, and Big Trouser. While you're still here, make sure to check our list of the hardest mobile games.

#4374. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 16, 2026

Welcome to spooky month where lawns suddenly grow giant skeletons, it's cold enough for a hoodie, the remakes of Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 released on Switch 2, and we're all prepping to hunker down for Winter. And Grand Theft Auto VI.

We're still in the thick of new release season which, fun fact, used to just be the month of November. But now it starts in August and ends in March, give or take a few weeks.

Before we get to our regularly scheduled weekend recommendations, though, here are some of the biggest Game Informer stories of the week.

It has been a long wait for a brand new Castlevania game, and frankly, I think Belmont's Curse has been worth the time spent in the queue. Charles Harte agrees, as he wrote in his review, "Belmont's Curse is a strong reminder of why the Castlevania series is so influential, with a rich world, tense combat, and a map chock-full of secrets. While this latest entry certainly pays homage to the Castlevanias of yore, it also breathes fresh life into the franchise, making me excited for its future. Castlevania is back, and between Rose Belmont and Evil Empire, it's in great hands."

The game comes from the team behind Dead Cells, a game heavily influenced by Castlevania to begin with, and the result shows how great a fit the team and franchise is. Controlling Rose Belmont feels great, the world is big and fun to explore without being overbearing, and beating each boss is a rewarding challenge. I often feel one mark of a good game for me is if it keeps me up past my bedtime, and Belmont's Curse is, unfortunately, doing a great job of making me feel tired all day. But that's a good thing.

The short pitch for Silver Pines is that it is a Metroid-inspired game crossed with a Silent Hill game. That's a good hook on its own, but what makes it stand out (at least in the limited time I have so far spent with it), is its animation. I don't know that it was actually rotoscoped (think the original 1989 Prince of Persia), but it feels like it was, which makes it look great and lends it an intentional level of uncanny valley that aids the creepy atmosphere. Throw in a dash of Twin Peaks energy, and you end up with something that feels unique against a sea of comparable (but often well-designed) Metroid-inspired games.

Just Dance is an frequent tradition in my household. We don't play it every year, but I was eager to check out Decades of Hits because of its included soundtrack. Just Dance generally leans on contemporary music and as a dad facing down his forties (who is still very cool, right? Right?!) I appreciate the chance to learn about recent pop hits and make a fool of myself in front of my family, but I like how musically diverse this entry is.

You have Sabrina Carpenter, Chappell Roan, and Olivia Rodrigo songs (which I adore), but you also get ABBA, Spice Girls, No Doubt, Daft Punk, Britney Spears, Sum 41, TLC, Gorillaz, Run DMC, Billy Joel, and Elton John among many others.

Also, in recent years, Just Dance has started its own tradition of including at least one shockingly impressive stop-motion animated sequence. I am not sure what executive at Ubisoft is accidentally approving the budget for the continued creation of these types of videos, but I hope they never notice because they're great.

You really can’t go wrong with any Jackbox game. Sure, there are some occasional duds in the packages, but there are always at least one or two super fun games that are always worth returning to. 12 is out this week and includes a game about sorting trivia questions into the right categories at high speed, one where you try to make the most ridiculous greeting card, a game encouraging silly debates, one that identifies connections among everyone playing, and finally Hyperface, where you manipulate selfies.

After an earlier release on VR platforms, the rhythm game Maestro recently made its way onto Switch and Switch 2, including a physical game cartridge launch. If you've always secretly loved the idea of stepping up onto the podium for a try at the conductor's gig, it's one worth tracking down. The game includes a number of classical hits from the likes of Beethoven, Vivaldi, and Tchaikovsky, but there's also the chance to play more contemporary tracks like those you'd hear in Star Wars or Game of Thrones. With Joy-Cons in hand, you'll keep the tempo, cue in musicians, adjust dynamics, and more. The accompanying visuals and "storytelling" aren't going to blow your mind, but the included music is hard to beat, and with occasional exceptions where the game misread my motions, I found the motion-tracking mostly up to the task of nailing the fantasy.

If you spent hours playing the early Toy Story games, then the retro compilation masters at Digital Eclipse have something for you in the form of Toy Story: Retro Roundup. On top of Toy Story, Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue, Toy Story 2, Buzz Lightyear of Star Command, and Toy Story Racer (including multiple versions of many of these), you can also get your hands on the 1998 A Bug's Life game. It may not have the breadth of extra content of something like Digital Eclipse's Atari 50 or Tetris Forever, but it's a fun stroll down memory lane with some behind-the-scenes interviews and materials. Alongside this retro collection, there's also the separate Toy Story 3 Complete Edition, also released by Digital Eclipse this week.

Kingdom Hearts Collection [I~III] – yes, that’s really what it’s called – is out on Nintendo Switch 2, and after spending some time with it, man, it feels right at home on the console. This collection includes Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 +2.5 ReMix (which itself includes a bunch of Kingdom Hearts games, including 1 and 2), Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue, and Kingdom Hearts III + Re Mind DLC. Basically, it has everything you need to catch up on the Kingdom Hearts saga before Kingdom Hearts IV launches next year.

As for actually playing these games, they feel amazing on Switch 2, courtesy of HD resolutions, on handheld and docked, and 60 FPS gameplay. I don’t know why exactly, but playing the Kingdom Hearts series on Switch 2 just feels right. It probably has something to do with just how many of these games were Nintendo console originals. Nonetheless, if you’re new to Kingdom Hearts or looking for a new place to tear up while "Dearly Beloved" plays, this Switch 2 collection will satisfy your needs.

This new standalone version of Forest Shuffle does more than transplant the theming into the Smoky Mountains of North America. It has also allowed its creators to refine balance, add new elements (like an intriguing new water/river terrain), create a more vibrant and visually beautiful presentation, and overall, up the value and playability of the game across the board. In short, it's what I think is the best version of an already very good game.

For newcomers, the Forest Shuffle formula is a card game that involves a mix of card hand management and tableau-building, as you slowly play out a forest scene onto the table, filled with unique trees, animals, and plants, and gathering points for the types and variety of things living in your woods. It's an approachable and visually enchanting game that still offers plenty of strategic depth as you plan out the shape and potential of your nature scene, all while planning against the impending arrival of winter.

#4373. 10 Weirdest Missions in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Gearbox has never shied away from adding weird characters and missions in their games. For instance, Borderlands 2 had a mission where your only goal was to shoot a guy named Face McShooty in the face.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

The developers rely on weird and unhinged comedy to help them sell the worlds they create, and Kairos is a rather interesting world with some interesting inhabitants that require your aid.

You might be tasked with proving that the world is flat, or maybe you need to go on a treasure hunt. No matter what though, you will be asked to perform some rather odd tasks in Borderlands 4.

Out in the Fadefields, you can find a missile that didn’t explode when it hit the ground. The missile’s name is Gigi, and she just wants to see if she can explode, as that is her purpose in life.

As you collect parts to rebuild the missile to place Gigi’s core into, she confides in you that she wishes to never be a dud. Through the mission, your vault hunter consoles Gigi, giving her hope that she may explode just like she wants.

In the end, you rebuild the rocket, fire it off into the distance, and let Gigi discover her one true purpose in life. It’s a weird mission to be sure, but a strangely hope-filled one that can touch the heart.

Have you ever taken a moment to think that the world might be flat? Well, there are many who have thought that, and many who still do, and Gearbox acknowledges that with the Flat Kairoser mission.

During this mission, you meet a guy named Skeptical Sam. He happens to be standing next to a vehicle with signs that read, “Kairos is flat,” and has a rather unique appearance.

Throughout the mission, you perform some interesting tasks to try and prove that Kairos is flat and not round like everyone else thinks. For instance, you smash a globe, and you travel to a shrine to see the “curvature” of Kairos. You are then required to prove that Kairos isn’t flat to completely debunk everything Sam believes.

Have you ever received a mission from a toilet with a sentient AI placed inside it? No? Well, you are about to, as that is what happens in the Potty Mouth mission in Borderlands 4.

GenIVIV from Borderlands 3 has made a return, and her AI has been placed inside of a toilet. She asks you to deal with miscreants around Carcadia Burn who mistreat her.

Once you talk to the mayor, however, you find out that GenIVIV has been a pain in the butt for everyone in the literal sense. After this, you must call upon ClapTrap with the Clap Signal and try to find a new body for GenIVIV. It is a hilariously strange quest with quite a few twists and turns.

The series is so brilliantly strange that it was difficult to choose the 10 Wildest Borderlands Side Quests.

Legendary singer Rodd Vomit, who you have obviously heard of, didn’t survive his crash landing onto Kairos. Therefore, the band Thrum Dumpster needs a new lead singer, and Lisa FullFolja needs you to track down some potential candidates.

You need to travel across Carcadia Burn to find a few different singers, attach Digi-Dongles to them, and then return to The Couch Hole. It’s a relatively straightforward mission, but it culminates in a musical mosh pit that makes it rather strange.

The band turns hostile, and you need to deal with it. It’s okay though, because Lisa reveals that was the plan all along, and that it was all done for clout.

You’ve heard of escape rooms before, but you’ve probably never experienced a no-escape room. It is a room that is designed to kill you if you get the answers wrong, and you need to help test it out.

You find the No-Escape Room mission in the Terminus District of Dominion, and it is a rather bizarre experience. Once you enter, the Smiley Man will have you attempt to complete the different rooms.

Of course, you can complete them the normal way, or you can cheat your way to victory. Along the way, you need to guess the correct door, go through a maze, and place symbols in order. All of this is done while a madman is talking to you.

Borderlands 4 has plenty of references to pop culture, and the Wayward Gun mission is one of them. It is also a bizarre quest that has you interacting with guns in a way you might not expect.

If you have ever wondered what it would be like to play Pokémon in Borderlands, then this mission is for you. After a group of Tediore weapons get loose, you are tasked with catching them all in storage containers.

You are given containers to throw like PokéBalls, and there is even a version of Team Rocket that appears to try and stop you. It is a surreal experience, but one that definitely stands out among the other missions in the game.

Borderlands may have bazillions of guns, but these ten are the weirdest ones around.

Do you remember Face McShooty in Borderlands 2? He was the guy that you need to shoot in the face. Well, there is a reference to this mission in Borderlands 4, and it is rather weird. Instead of shooting a guy, you crack a guy’s back.

In Terminus Range, you can come across a man named Crack McBacky, and you need to crack his back as the name of the mission implies. However, the crick in his back is rather persistent, and won’t be dealt with easily.

Throughout the mission, you need to consistently melee his back. Just when you think he has received the relief he wants, you need to crack it again. This keeps going until you jump off a literal cliff and slam his back.

Have you ever thought that maybe your calling in life was to help others receive spiritual enlightenment? Well, that is what you are trying out in the Next Quest Thing mission in Borderlands 4.

A Wayward Soul wants you to help give them spiritual guidance. Of course, you are not a guru of any sort, so you will need to improvise. During the mission, you make up a lot of different tasks for the Wayward Soul to complete to give him spiritual enlightenment.

He wants balance, so you balance a trash can lid on his head. At a certain point, the guy even tries to be friends with a Ripper.

Sure, murder, mayhem, and chaos are all fun, but they get stale after a while. Sometimes, you need to find something else to do on Kairos, so why not try out some practical jokes?

That is the premise of the Imminent Jest mission, as you are recruited to help a Ripper perform some little pranks. Jankus wants to prank Crankus, so you shoot a pipe to get ooze all over Crankus.

Of course, now it is Crankus’ turn to prank Jankus … by setting him on fire. These harmless pranks don’t turn out to be so harmless, but it is a weird quest that takes a bit of a break from the nonstop violence of Borderlands 4, making it memorable and strange.

At a certain point in your travels around Kairos, you may come across a man surrounded by Threshers. This man is named Mort, and he has a desire to breed some Threshers, and you need to help him out with this strange request.

First, you are tasked with collecting a few Thresher eggs. This isn’t the weird part. The weird part comes when you get back to Mort’s shack and see that it is covered in hearts. It even has a sign that reads, “Hump hut.”

After delivering the eggs, he hatches one, calls the Thresher Daisy, and then proceeds to tell you to help her attract a mate. From here on out, it is weird, there is mood music involved, and plenty of pulsating tentacles. Gearbox got weird with this one.

Pop culture references are a baked-in part of the Borderlands games, but these ten are the greatest.

#4372. 8 Elden Ring Details That Suggest Some of the Biggest Mysteries Still Aren’t Solved

Melissa Sarnowski is a Gaming Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in lists, reviews, and features, with additional experience writing guides for Hardcore Gamer. Before joining DualShockers, Melissa contributed to Screen Rant, and she currently writes for CBR and

Elden Ring is weird, and I mean that in the best way. FromSoftware builds elaborate worlds in each game the developers make, and the effort and attention to detail that goes into those worlds mean that you can spend dozens of hours digging into the lore and still not have a clear idea of it.

Bored with the way you go about your journey in The Lands Between? Here are the 10 best ways to make your second Elden Ring playthrough different.

This design for lore also means that you likely won't find an answer to every question. If you're like me, then the mystery is part of the charm. It keeps you wondering, and that keeps you playing as you search for answers that might not fully exist in-game in as straightforward of a way as you’d wish.

My favorite mystery is the Gloam-Eyed Queen. You never get to see her, but multiple items refer to her, and you learn that she was the main rival of Marika. It's also heavily implied that she still has some followers in the Lands Between.

However, we don't know her real identity, what happened to her, or where she is if she's alive. One interesting theory is that Melina is the Gloam-Eyed Queen due to her one eye seeming sealed shut, but when it's open in the Frenzied Flame ending, it has a gloam color to it.

This is a bit interesting because we know why the Land of Shadow was separated from the Lands Between. Marika effectively sealed away her past in the Land of Shadow, but more importantly, she was able to block access to the exact gate that let her ascend to godhood. Of course, she would put measures in place that prevented others from getting power like that.

The mystery is how she separated it and how Miquella was able to create an entrance that others could follow him through. However, the methods aren't exactly important enough to impact the lore much, and we just don't know the extent of Marika’s abilities.

Aside from its name, there are multiple mentions of locations beyond the Lands Between. We also know that the Tarnished, when they had their Grace removed by Marika, were sent away and returned later. So, that means that the Lands Between is a place that can be accessed from other lands.

It also raises the question as to why the Lands Between is so unique and has the Erdtree and, previously, the Crucible. Are the other lands not worth the attention of the Outer Gods, or is it just that the gods we know of aren't interested, but others might be? There's just not enough information to find an answer.

The Greater Will is well-known, and a few gods like the God of Rot, Formless Mother, and Frenzied Flame are mentioned enough that we know they exist and have some interest in the Lands Between. However, we really don't know much about the gods or what they want from this land.

These Elden Ring bosses are underrated and deserve more praise.

It's obvious that the Erdtree is what they're after, but the Erdtree is almost certainly built on the Crucible, which could be another goal or the main goal. But the Greater Will apparently has the ability to create and defeat gods, so it seems strange that it would want power from the Lands Between unless it's to keep it out of the hands of other gods.

Nokstella alone is filled with so much mystery that it's difficult to condense into a summary when you need a ton of context and explanations. Honestly, you could write a novella on the many unanswered questions that come from this location.

The Nox, who built Nokstella after rebelling against the Greater Will unsuccessfully, were originally thought to be connected to the Numen and Marika, but the DLC puts Marika in a completely different location. But then you have the connections between the Black Knives and Marika, along with the Black Knives being connected to the Nox. There are too many threads and almost no answers here.

Placidusax has two heads when you encounter him for his boss fight, but he also has a few stumps where more heads once were. The story is that his missing heads were cut off by Bayle, and you can find that two of his heads are with Bayle when you see him in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC.

Except that's not accounting for every head. Placidusax has two remaining. Bayle has two of the missing ones, but if you look at Placidusax’s model and the Old Lord's Talisman, it shows that he should have five heads. The problem is that we have no idea what happened to the fifth one.

There are seven walking mausoleums in Elden Ring, and we can assume that they were made by the Nox because of their design, which matches the buildings in Nokstella, a style found nowhere else. The interesting part is that we're told they house soulless demigods, so those in the same state as Godwyn.

If that's true, then the bodies in them must be Marika’s children. A ghost even tells you when talking about one that it has Marika's unwanted child in it. When you start Elden Ring, you feel like you know who Marika's children are, but the details of the world let you know that she apparently had far more children than you think as you dig into the lore.

I'm fascinated by the Gate of Divinity, and I think it's one of the most well-known mysteries if you played the DLC or even watched the trailer for it. This is where Marika ascended to godhood, and Miquella later followed in her footsteps, albeit with a much shorter reign since you end it immediately.

Yet we know nothing about this gate other than the fact that it grants divinity. There seem to be requirements for being able to use it successfully, but beyond that we don't know how or why it works. We don't even know where it connects to.

FromSoftware makes such fascinating games that leave you thinking about them even years after they were released, encouraging you to explore every bit of content. Unfortunately, like most of their games, we're probably not going to get answers for every mystery in Elden Ring.

FromSoftware games are full of many NPCs, but many of them are hurt by your intervention, and not helped. Here are the best/saddest examples.

The 2022 action RPG by From Software joins the Souls-like subgenre by presenting one of the most punishing games in the field with grotesque, memorable bosses to keep you up at night. Inside a world built by Hidetaka Miyazaki and Game of Thrones writer George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring's gothic landscape, unforgiving combat, and top-tier exploration will keep you invested well into the year.

#4371. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

After a lower bracket run in São Paulo, the LATAM squad claimed the #VCTGameChangers Championship trophy! pic.twitter.com/YeSeb10TZc

— VCT Pacific (@vctpacific) November 1, 2026

The São Paulo final also closes a format. KRÜ are the last team to lift the trophy at a separate event of its own. For the first time, the Game Changers Championship will finish at Champions. Under Riot’s 2027 plan, non-partner teams that qualify for the Game Changers Championship will receive an extra US0,000 incentive. VALORANT Champions 2027 is scheduled for 16 September to 10 October in Austin.

#4370. Pokémon Masters EX tier list - The best sync pairs to use

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version:  2.74.0 - Latest Additions:  Arc Suit Hau & Raichu, Arc Suit Gladion & Silvally, Maxie (Fall 2026) & Ting-Lu

With over 200 collectable Sync Pairs of Pokémon and their masters, it sure can get confusing for new players and veterans alike to come to a definitive conclusion about which ones are the best and which ones they should avoid. Pokémon Masters EX, the officially licensed game by DeNA, has brought tons of new Sync Pairs for players to collect and use with their fifth anniversary. This Pokémon Masters EX tier list is here to serve as a curated list of Sync Pairs that can help you in your journey of becoming the best Pokémon trainer.

You will find all the answers in this tier list as to whether a certain Sync Pair is better or worse than another. Keep in mind that tier lists are inherently subjective in nature. Use your own judgment while investing your resources in these Sync Pairs, but feel free to take inspiration from them.

Stay tuned for the updated versions of this tier list - we will make sure to add new Sync Pairs as they are released while also adjusting the individual categories based on future balance adjustments.

Let’s get you right to our Pokémon Masters EX tier list!

The main focus of judging Sync Pairs in this tier list will be mostly on their damage-dealing capabilities. Most of the Sync Pairs here have striking abilities that help them deal more damage. Of course, some exceptions exist, like the Steven & Deoxys (Attack Forme) Sync Pair that can also boost the critical hit rate of all allies. However, that's just an added bonus to their already high damage multipliers and potential value.

Some of the most notable damage dealers are going to be Red & Pikachu, Lucas & Dialga, and Steven & Deoxys (Attack Forme). Red & Pikachu's special move B Thunderbolt is a massive hyper-scaling damaging move that increases its own damage the more it is used. Such moves are not only good in PvE content where fights can drag out, but also in certain PvP situations against tanky stall team comps. Lucas & Dialga is possibly the best Dragon-type Sync Pair available due to their special move Dragon Zone that can boost the stats of all Dragon-types. Steven & Deoxys (Attack Forme) is the ultimate counter to Sync Pairs that reduce the stats of enemies. Their passive ability, Downside Up, states that whenever an enemy reduces the stats of Steven and Deoxys (Attack Forme), the move instead increases their stats by the same amount. Simply pop in to our store, purchase the game at our midnight opening, and receive a replica box, inner tray and key ring.

This slipcase, as shown in the image below, will allow you to store the Switch 2 version of the game inside of it. The one catch is it's "only instore" at the Argos Tottenham Court Road store during this event, and "whilst stocks last".

If you're attending this event, you'll also be able to play the Switch 2 in-store, shop for exclusive Nintendo merch and browse the latest games and accessories.

Similar offers have been revealed elsewhere. In Canada, EB Games is offering its own version of the classic N64 box art. If you want to find out where else to pre-order the game, you can check out our guide here on Nintendo Life.

#4367. HoYoverse's Petit Planet Launches in December, Switch 2 Port Coming 2027

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

In the gacha gaming scene, HoYoverse, international division of Chinese game developer miHoYo, has become one of the definitive faces, offering games like the high-grossing Genshin Impact, the stylish Zenless Zone Zero, and my personal favorite gacha game, Honkai: Star Rail. Even as new challengers constantly appear in the gacha scene, and there are a lot of them, HoYo maintains a powerful presence thanks to its games, and especially its character designs.

We were able to get some extensive time with HoYoverse's upcoming life simulator, Petit Planet, and were left grinning from ear-to-ear.

While all of its other games are merrily chugging along, HoYo is still working on even more titles to add to its catalog and appeal to an even larger variety of potential players. One such title is Petit Planet, a life sim game in a similar vein to titles like Animal Crossing. Petit Planet has run several beta tests since its initial announcement in September of last year, and it seems HoYo is finally ready to launch the proverbial rocket.

In a pre-launch special program that aired over the weekend, HoYo officially revealed Petit Planet’s global launch date as December 4, 2026. As is typical for HoYo games, it’ll be launching on PC, both via HoYo’s own HoYoPlay launcher and the Epic Games Store, and mobile devices via Android and iOS. However, in a first for HoYo, the game will also be launching on the Switch 2, albeit in 2027 after the initial launch, as announced today on a post to the game’s official X, formerly Twitter account.

Several of HoYo’s other titles, primarily Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero, have been made available on gaming consoles before, with their primary affinity being the PlayStation 4 and, later, PlayStation 5, though Genshin and ZZZ specifically also made it over to the XBOX Series X/S. However, none of the developer’s titles have made it to either the Nintendo Switch or Switch 2, at least until now.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is shaping up to be a stand-out monster taming game from HoYoverse.

The post on the official Petit Planet X that announced the Switch 2 port didn’t specify when, exactly, we’ll be seeing this port beyond a broad window of 2027, but it is still an interesting addition to HoYo’s wheelhouse, and hopefully a sign that its other titles are on the way as well. Maybe we can start getting  more Star Rail crossovers…

None of the developer’s titles have made it to either the Nintendo Switch or Switch 2, at least until now.

Even if you plan on playing the game on the Switch 2, you might want to make your account ahead of time anyway, as due to the large number of pre-registrations the game received during its developmental period, there will be a swath of rewards for all players upon initial log-in. All players will receive 2 Blissful Floral & Fruit Tea, 2 Red Star Fireworks, 2 Sweet Specials, 100 Bazaar Jelly, the Sproutling Outfit, and the Bestie Star Light.

With this latest announcement, it’s shaping up to be quite the winter season for those interested in gacha games. Following Petit Planet’s launch on December 4, an entirely new gacha game, Silver Palace, will be launching a little over a week later on December 14 for PC, PS5, Android, and iOS, as that game’s developers announced a couple of days ago.

NetEase Games and Naked Rain revealed a brand-new trailer for Ananta during ONL's gamescom.

Not only that, but the following month, the long-anticipated city sandbox gacha game Ananta will be launching on January 15, 2027 for PS5, Android, iOS, and PC specifically via Steam, as opposed to Petit Planet and Silver Palace’s places on the Epic Games Store outside of dedicated clients.

It’s also worth a reminder that HoYo, in particular, still has a lot of irons in the fire even with Petit Planet officially poised for launch. The most recent test for its creature battling game, Honkai: Nexus Anima, ran this past summer, while one of its other new brand-new IPs, Nodusfall, was announced at Gamescom back in August, showing a much darker fantasy aesthetic compared to the more anime-based stylings of Genshin, ZZZ, and the Honkai games.

#4366. Dead Cells weapons tier list - every weapon ranked

Not sure which melee weapon, ranged weapon, grenade, turret, or trap to bring? We've got you covered.

Updated on November 3rd, 2026 - Version 3.5.15

Dead Cells has a lot of weapons, making it perfect for a tier list ranking every weapon. Throughout the game, you'll come across melee weapons, ranged weapons, traps, turrets, and even grenades, each with different effects like damage over time or freezing an enemy in their place. It can feel a little overwhelming, even though they're often slow or difficult to unlock and discover.

That's where our Dead Cells weapons tier list comes in. While we haven't gone into detail about most of the weapons here, we wanted to give you a quick overview of the best, the brightest, and, of course, most destructive tools in your arsenal to help you survive this perilous world.

Which weapons should you unlock in Dead Cells? It's a tough question, isn't it? You only have limited cells to spend on unlocking blueprints, so picking the best weapons to unlock can be tricky and overwhelming. We recommend starting with our S-tier weapons and working your way down from there. Most are ranked by their base damage numbers, but where a weapon or skill does something special and interesting, we've made sure to note it.

Of course, ultimately, it all comes down to personal preference. Make sure you read every weapon's description and decide if it would suit you. Some weapons have extra effects like applying a damage-over-time effect, like Bleed, or even combining with other weapons to create a one-two punch kind of effect. It's all personal. Dead Cells weapons tier list So, without further ado, let's get down to business. We've taken the time to break everything down by type for you: melee weapons, ranged weapons, shields (yes, they count), turrets and traps, and grenades. Each has its place in battle. Each will help you in some way to reach the end of the road.

If you disagree with anything on this list, then please let us know in the comments! These are a matter of opinion, after all, aside from their ranking on base damage. Critical damage is also important, so be sure to read the weapon description to take that into account.

Melee weapons make up the bread and butter of your arsenal, comprising everything from swords and axes to a spiked wrecking ball and a giant shark. Yes, a shark. Here, we've gone through and listed every melee weapon, ranked according to base damage.

Some weapons stand out more than others, of course. The Ferryman's Lantern allows you to kill an enemy to gather its soul. Then, as a secondary attack, charge it to fire those souls as projectiles, dealing critical hits if three souls are shot at the same time. With a base damage of 164 plus secondary damage of 107, then critical hits applying 429 damage, this is a monster of a weapon.

Others stand out for their usefulness and fun factor. With the Maw of the Deep, your third attack throws the shark, rooting the enemy and inflicting bleed. Rooted targets will then take critical damage - 158 base, and 270 critical.

The Rapier allows you to critical hit immediately after a roll or parry, and if you play the game like us, you'll be rolling around a lot anyway. With the Meat Skewer, your first attack places you behind the enemy, with your second hit applying critical damage. The Pure Nail comes courtesy of fellow Metroidvania Hollow Knight, allowing you to attack while moving left, right, and up. Drop down on an enemy and attack downwards to "bounce," just like in Hollow Knight, applying damage while in the air.

Finally, the Hard Light Sword is actually two weapons in one, along with the Hard Light Gun. A reference to the acclaimed Hyper Light Drifter, these weapons work in tandem. Fire the Hard Light Gun into enemies to damage and mark them. Then, the Hard Light Sword deals critical damage based on the number of shots it has received. Sword hits also recharge ammo for the gun, which (unlike other ranged weapons, more on those next) doesn't recharge over time. It's an elegant dance that might not be the most powerful, but is undoubtedly one of the most fun tools in the Dead Cells weapons arsenal.

Time for the first of our tier lists, then! Here we go: Rank Weapon S Ferryman's Lantern, Cursed Sword, War Spear, Tombstone, Flint, Oven Axe, Wrecking Ball, Giantkiller, Vampire Killer, Bible, Alucard's Sword, Death's Scythe, Misericorde A Toothpick, Symmetrical Lance, Shrapnel Axes, Hattori's Katana, Meat Skewer, Broadsword, Impaler, Crowbar, Twin Daggers, Hayabusa Boots, Vorpan, Shovel, Maw of the Deep, Rapier, Baseball Bat, Nutcracker, Pure Nail, Morning Star, Whip Sword, Sewing Scissors B Balanced Blade, Flashing Fans, Spite Sword, Rusty Sword, Bone, Swift Sword, Frantic Sword, Iron Staff, Assassin's Dagger, Rhythm n' Bouzouki, Seismic Strike, Wrenching Whip, Oiled Sword, Hayabusa Gauntlets, Blood Sword, Panchaku, Gold Digger, Machete and Pistol, Hard Light Sword, Giant Comb C Flawless, Sadist's Stiletto, Valmont's Whip, Torch, Abyssal Trident, Hand Hook, Spiked Boots, Bladed Tonfas, Dagger of Profit, Snake Fangs, Scythe Claw, Tentacle, King Scepter, Queen's Rapier, Starfury, Spartan Sandals

Ranged weapons are extremely helpful in Dead Cells, especially when you don't want to get close to an enemy. Most use ammunition that regenerates over time, or can be retrieved from enemies on death or following a successful parry, in the case of arrows. Some, like the combined Hard Light Sword and Gun mentioned on the previous page, have a special function - in this case, ammo doesn't recharge passively and instead must be recharged by landing hits with the Hard Light Sword.

Here's how we ranked the Dead Cells tier list for ranged weapons. Rank Weapon S Money Shooter, Ice Crossbow, Throwable Objects, Heavy Crossbow, Multiple-nocks Bow, Sonic Carbine, Barrel Launcher, Fire Blast, Magic Missiles, Medusa's Head, Anathema, Laser Glaive A Chakram of the Queen, The Boy's Axe, Peril Glyphs, Boomerang, Explosive Crossbow, Bow and Endless Quiver, Repeater Crossbow, Quick Bow, Laser Glaive, Gilded Yumi, Blowgun, Marksman's Bow, Ice Shards, Cross, Throwing Axe B Electric Whip, Lightning Bolt, War Javelin, Pyrotechnics, Nerves of Steel, Infantry Bow, Killing Deck, Hemorrhage C Beginner's Bow, Frost Blast, Ice Bow Firebrands, Hokuto's Bow, Magic Bow, Throwing Knife, Alchemic Carbine

Shields might be a boring choice for your adventure through Dead Cells, but don't sleep on them. Hold down a shield's assigned button to hold it up after 0.37 seconds. Attacks that hit the front are reduced by the shield's damage absorption percentage, typically around 75%, while also dealing damage to the enemy by the damage number listed on the shield.

Shields can also be used to parry attacks. Tap the button rather than hold it down, and it attempts a parry. If no attack hits during that window, you can't block or parry again for a little under a second. If your parry is successful, then a few things can happen: you can parry or block again immediately and enjoy an additional effect, depending on the attack.

Carrying a shield also passively creates a force field for 0.5 seconds after you take damage, absorbing most damage except DoT effects like poison and some enemy attacks.

Here, we've ranked shields in Dead Cells by their base block damage, meaning the damage the enemy takes after you block an attack. As always, read the shield's in-game description for any interesting effects, like AoE damage. Rank Weapon S Spiked Shield, Greed Shield, Punishment, Knockback Shield, Alucard's Shield A Force Shield, Thunder Shield, Assault Shield, Front Line Shield, Ice Shield B Rampart, Bloodthirsty Shield C Old Wooden Shield, Cudgel, Parry Shield

Deployable skills in Dead Cells come in three forms: traps and turrets, grenades, and various miscellaneous powers. It isn't possible to start with these skills without the Recycling Tubes upgrade.

First, let's cover deployable skills like traps and turrets. These come in powered and unpowered forms. Powered skills, such as turrets, need you to remain within their proximity for them to function. Line of sight is best, with the effective radius decreased if blocked by terrain. As long as you're within proximity, though, you'll notice a line of electricity connecting you to the deployed skill, allowing it to function.

Unpowered deployable skills are typically traps that don't actively attack on your behalf, such as traps that activate when the enemy steps onto them.

Let's rank the various types of deployable skills. First up, turrets. The Sinew Slicer is particularly worth noting. You'll come across it early, and it makes short work of early enemies without placing you in danger. Rank Skill S Barnacle, Scavenged Bombard, Heavy Turret, Cleaver A Double Crossb-o-matic, Sinew Slicer B Tesla Coil C Flamethrower Turret

Next up, traps and miscellaneous powers. The Emergency Door skill simply spawns a door in front of you, which acts like a regular door, meaning it can be destroyed to stun enemies on the other side. The Night Light is extremely situational and can be deployed in the Forgotten Sepulcher to help with the Darkness. Requiring 120 seconds to recharge, it can be thrown to a location to create a temporary light at that location. Touch it to replenish your light aura. Rank Skill S Crusher A Explosive Decoy B Wolf Trap C Night Light, Emergency Door

Grenades in Dead Cells do exactly what you expect: they explode. What more could you want? Simply throw, and enjoy! Some have added effects, of course, and can be paired with other skills or weapons for greater use. The Ice Grenade freezes enemies, for example, and the Root Grenade roots enemies, causing damage over time and keeping them rooted. The Magnetic Grenade is useful in crowded rooms. After a few moments, it attracts enemies in a large area, then explodes to deal electrical damage over time.

Grenades, like other skills, aren't exactly consumables as you would expect in other games. Rather they each have a set cooldown, meaning they can be reused over and over again.

The Hunter's Grenade is situational, which is why it's ranked C, but it's quite useful at the same time. Throw it to "annoy" a monster. When its health drops to 40% or less, use "Blueprint Extractor" to grab a blueprint. Rank Skill S Powerful Grenade, Holy Water A Infantry Grenade, Cluster Grenade, Magnetic Grenade B Stun Grenade, Ice Grenade, Fire Grenade, Root Grenade, Oil Grenade, Swarm C Hunter's Grenade
