Last week, EA shut down Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare, which resulted in the cancellation of the fifth Mass Effect game that was announced in 2020. As the fallout from this closure settles, famed video game composer Austin Wintory has shared that he'd been working on a potential soundtrack for the now-canceled game and has publicly released early versions of this score.

In a Bluesky thread, Wintory, who has composed soundtracks for games such as Journey, Sword of the Sea (for which he won a Grammy), Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate, and The Banner Saga trilogy, writes, “Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project. For the last couple years I'd been in discussion w/ BioWare & EA to take on the project & as part of that I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next, may as well share it!"

Wintory uploaded a 20-minute video consisting of eight tracks to his YouTube channel. The video begins with a message further elaborating on the partnership between BioWare, EA, and him. “For the past several years, I’d been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5. As part of these conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a gigantic love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next.”

Wintory adds that he composed the music in 2025 and that he “knew nothing” about what Mass Effect 5's story entailed when he did. As such, he describes the music as “narratively speculative.” He adds that this conceptual soundtrack was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick’s soundtrack on the first Mass Effect “while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix),” he writes. Each music track features a message by Wintory explaining his inspiration for its production.

“Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," Wintory writes in the video's description. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever. Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much.”

Wintory's music is the latest piece of potential Mass Effect 5 content to emerge since BioWare’s closure. A day after the shutdown announcement, an unreleased but reportedly legitimate cinematic trailer for the canceled Mass Effect leaked online.

#4283. Aonuma Calls the Water Temple His 'Overdue Homework' for Ocarina of Time Remake

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

With the release of the full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo Switch 2 later this week, old-school fans have been once again reminiscing on their many fond and not-so-fond memories from the N64 original. Whenever the topic of Ocarina of Time comes up, it’s often a safe bet that, sooner or later, things will turn to the infamous Water Temple, one of the elemental-themed dungeons in the game’s back half.

The Water Temple has long held a reputation for being one of the most legendarily frustrating dungeons in the Zelda franchise. Admittedly, a lot of the discourse is hyperbolic, based on memories of collective childhood, but the dungeon also definitely had some irritating quirks, from its confusing layout to the way it forced you to use your items and menus. If you didn’t have the little jingle that played every time you opened the pause menu permanently seared into your head before that dungeon, you sure did afterward.

The first gameplay trailer for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has confirmed that it has added a beloved feature from the 3DS version.

The designers of the Ocarina of Time remake are very aware of the long-standing vibe toward the Water Temple, as they discussed in an Ask the Developer feature on Nintendo’s official blog. Eiji Aonuma, the director and dungeon designer of the original game, now a senior officer and producer on the remake, spoke on how he created the original dungeon and how his perspective has changed since, with the remake’s director, Hokwai Ng, discussing how they’re making improvements without changing the fundamental vibe of the dungeon.

As part of the interview, Aonuma, Ng, and other members of the development team were asked how they approached the development of dungeons in the Ocarina of Time remake, particularly in relation to the original.

With a laugh, Aonuma said, “I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago.” He said that, back in the days of the N64, there were very few games that allowed you to do much of anything in an underwater setting. Therefore, if he was going to make an underwater dungeon, he wanted it to be distinct, something that brings across what could make being in such an environment fun. Aonuma is actually a hobbyist freediver, so he’s very acquainted with the distinct sensations of being completely underwater.

If he was going to make an underwater dungeon, he wanted it to be distinct, something that brings across what could make being in such an environment fun.

However, he concedes that the biggest problem with the Water Temple was one of navigation. “With the dungeon’s complex structure and a lot of item toggling involved, you often had to open the menu screen repeatedly, making it hard to keep track of where you were and which way you were facing.”

A look at the Water Temple from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and how it should be remade with the same design.

Aonuma explained that, given the infamy that the Water Temple has accrued due to its difficulty, he had the dev team make some adjustments, not necessarily to make it flat-out easier, but to make it more playable and user-friendly.

Ng chimed in here to explain the team’s perspective, noting that most of the dungeon’s basic mechanisms have been preserved, but the layout has been slightly shifted in places to improve the overall signposting and flow of the dungeon. Additionally, some of the walls of the temple have been changed to a distinct lattice pattern, allowing you to see bits of the temple beyond the current room and get a better idea of where you are in relation to everything else, which will hopefully keep players from getting lost. Finally, item toggling has been streamlined, so you don’t need to keep opening the menu to equip and unequip your Iron Boots.

Are you excited for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake? So are we! Here are 8 changes we would like to see implemented in the remake.

At the end of the interview, Ng added that he hopes the slight differences between the remake and the original will spark some inter-generational conversation. He imagined a father playing the game with his child and saying, “You know, your Dad got stuck in the Water Temple plenty of times back in the day.”

Aonuma laughed and responded, “Then kids playing this version might say, “Come on, it’s not that hard.” Poor old Dad might end up feeling deflated.”

#4281. Free-To-Play MOBA Pokémon Unite Is Shutting Down In March

The free-to-play MOBA Pokémon Unite will shut down in March, over five years after its 2021 launch. Although a gradual suspension of services begins today, fans will enjoy one last hurrah thanks to a big in-game event running for the remainder of the game’s lifecycle.

Launched in July 2021 for Switch before migrating to iOS and Android later that year, Pokémon Unite was billed as a friendlier take on the MOBA genre popularized by Dota 2 and League of Legends, thanks to its short matches (10 minutes) and simplified mechanics. Despite its initial popularity, the game is winding down and will go offline for good on March 23, 2027.

An End of Service notice on the game’s website reads,

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021. We would like to express our thanks to everyone by holding a special event until service ends. The Pokémon Unite Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament (an event for Pokémon Unite only) will also be held as previously announced. We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service. After service ends, the 'Pokémon Unite Game Content Guidelines for Online Platforms' will no longer be published or maintained, and we will no longer provide support regarding use of Pokémon Unite videos and images.”

As of today, in-game sales of Aeos gems and Unite Club memberships/renewals have been suspended. Existing Unite Club members will continue to use their benefits until the end of the membership period.

On November 12, an update will kick off the aforementioned final special event, where players can obtain items such as all Unite licenses and Holoware that have appeared in the game up to that point. A library feature will also be added, letting players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down on March 23. Those who don’t download the library feature before the shutdown date will not be able to get it afterward.

Qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo Competitive tournament will take place as planned on December 5. After the game shuts down on March 23, players won't be able to log in to Pokémon Unite or play any battles. Only the library feature will remain accessible.

We enjoyed Pokémon Unite when it launched, with executive video editor Alex Van Aken scoring it an 8 out of 10 in his review, writing, “The game eats away the hours of my day as I reassuringly say to myself, 'Just one more match.' Battles play out with the spectacle that the Pokémon series is known for, and with so many abilities to choose from, no match feels the same as the last. The game’s simple mechanics and recognizable characters make for an approachable MOBA experience, and with a potential catalog of nearly 900 Pokémon to pick from, my hopes are high for the future of Pokémon Unite.”

We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

#4278. 10 Action-Adventure Games That Are Unexpected Masterpieces

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

The action-adventure genre is one of the broadest in the entire video game industry, encompassing countless experiences ranging from stealth and hack-and-slash to horror and beat 'em ups.

Thanks to this broad definition, countless masterpieces fall under its umbrella, including many that, unfortunately, haven't achieved the popularity they deserve due to fierce competition.

Even within the realm of major blockbusters, not all underrated titles are obscure indie games—there are games that have fallen just short of mainstream success, though I'm here to help rectify that.

So, in order to shed light on some lesser-known campaigns that haven't yet cemented their undeniable excellence in the collective consciousness, I invite you to explore this list of ten action-adventure games that are unexpected masterpieces.

As the least recognized work from Tango Gameworks, a studio that has certainly gifted us with numerous magnificent journeys, Ghostwire: Tokyo stands out among the games with the greatest disparity between its quality and its fame.

Boasting one of the finest atmospheres crafted this decade, wandering the streets of Shibuya, soaring across rooftops, and taking down the most terrifying yokai imaginable is, by far, one of my highlights of the decade.

Whether in stealth or direct magical combat, tackling one of its turbulent side quests or hunting for collectibles, the game strikes an outstanding balance between making each mechanic satisfying while still maintaining a constant sense of terror in its setting.

As far as first-person games go, Ghostwire: Tokyo is part of the most immersive, rewarding, and distinctive I've played this generation, which is saying something considering the titans with which it shares category.

As the years have gone by, games that adhere to the Metroidvania philosophy have become one of my greatest obsessions, which inevitably led me to fall in love with Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo.

Its ability to capture the nostalgia of the Game Boy Advance era while boasting the refined design and execution of modern products demonstrates its creators' immeasurable talent, who also imbued it with an impressive thematic personality.

The critiques of various strategic production industries resonate with our current times, while in the process, the game leverages the yoyo as a central gameplay element to make traversal, combat, exploration, and customization an absolute delight that's also pretty unique.

Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo is among the finest indie titles I've enjoyed in the last couple of years, and anything other than recognizing it as brilliant is to underestimate its potential.

If you're interested in unfairly criticized titles, I recommend checking out these ten underrated action-adventure games that were badly reviewed.

As someone who didn't experience the franchise's heyday, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance not only caught me completely off guard, but I can think of very few resurrections that have felt so powerful.

The absolute masterwork of action and platforming that this title is results in frankly mind-blowing sequences, flowing seamlessly between both dimensions to deliver a thrilling adventure that doesn't let you breathe for a second.

As you unlock combos, powers, and movement abilities, you encounter an ever-increasing series of challenges that push the game's mechanics to their limits, which are meticulously refined to ensure you have complete control over every pixel.

Few titles in 2025 felt as satisfying to complete 100%, so Shinobi: Art of Vengeance stands as a masterfully unexpected example that, when you don't know what to do with your old IPs, outsourcing to an indie studio to work on them is the best possible idea.

The Legend of Zelda's heirs number in the hundreds of thousands, but that didn't stop Death's Door from emerging as one of its most intelligent and charismatic great-great-grandchildren.

The game perfectly understands the enjoyment that lies in discovery and exploration through iteration, inviting us on a diverse adventure with plenty of colorful biomes, enemies, characters, and circumstances that evoke all kinds of emotions.

Curiosity, fear, happiness, sadness, worry... The title silently manages a multitude of emotions both thematically and in its gameplay, limiting progression to allow for exploration of its expansive world at a prodigious pace.

When discussing isometric titles that combine action, platforming, and puzzles in the best possible way, Death's Door is at the description's forefront, though it's the ease and finesse with which it achieves this that's truly unexpected.

Castlevania is a series that went through some difficult years after the turn of the century, and it wasn't until Castlevania: Lords of Shadow arrived that the IP unexpectedly found some relief amidst so many setbacks, astonishingly becoming the best-selling game in the entire IP.

MercurySteam crafted one of the most beautiful and satisfying hack-and-slash games in the genre's history, finally adapting the saga's formula perfectly to 3D without losing an ounce of its core identity.

The whip feels better than ever, as do the movement mechanics, the puzzles, and the progression systems, all enhanced in the best possible way thanks to a magnificently crafted story and characters that keep you on the edge of your seat until the very last second.

Castlevania: Lords of Shadow completely forgoes being conceptually innovative, but the sacrifice, given it guaranteed us an extremely excellent title in all its facets, was totally worth it even when nobody was betting on such a resounding success.

If you enjoy discovering incredible titles without proper recognition, I recommend these ten best action-adventure games forgotten by time.

In the years when God of War slowed down, and Devil May Cry practically disappeared, a third icon emerged from absolutely nowhere to keep the hack-and-slash genre alive (with Bayonetta's permission): Darksiders.

Drawing inspiration from both Santa Monica Studio's work and The Legend of Zelda, Vigil Games crafted a splendidly elaborate tale and setting within Judeo-Christian mythology, one of the least explored in the video game industry.

Giant bosses based on satisfying gimmicks, varied and refreshing puzzles that make the most of War's arsenal and movement capabilities, phenomenal art design for both environments and enemies... It's the complete package.

That the company's first title would be such a presentation of knowledge in the genre's fundamentals was unforeseen even for the team itself, but much more for the hundreds of thousands who, like me, stumbled upon Darksiders by chance and have been hooked ever since.

Returning to the topic of franchises forced to reinvent themselves to adapt to modern times, not even the most optimistic projections for the Tomb Raider reboot could have predicted the absolute brilliance it would become.

Going back to Lara Croft's origins resulted in one of the quintessential action-adventure games of the entire generation, achieving an astonishing symphony of survival mechanics, realistic yet compelling gunplay, and simply fantastic settings and stories.

Each set piece surpasses the last, and the spectacular scenery contrasts perfectly with the brutal and tense story the legendary archaeologist faces, all while possessing the intriguing premise of not yet being the intrepid adventurer we all know, but rather a young, still-innocent graduate.

From concept to execution, Tomb Raider is a tapestry of sound decisions that, among other things, reminded Uncharted fans that Nathan Drake only managed to run because Lara Croft walked first.

I know that nowadays we're used to indie masterpieces being released every couple of months, but back in the day, before that was the norm, Hyper Light Drifter arrived like a hurricane of grandeur.

Taking Dark Souls' harshness, non-linearity, and disorientation, Heart Machine assembled an adventure that is both cryptic and captivating, where the gameplay and narrative direction are entirely in the player's hands.

Where to go and why are questions that only the user can answer through exploration, embarking on an intense and introspective journey where bosses and secrets abound, motivating us to explore every last corner of its silent world.

Along with gorgeous pixel art, a remarkable sound design, and a simple yet perfect gameplay loop, Hyper Light Drifter built a castle with just a few blocks, a feat reserved only for the greatest.

If you're looking for modern games to get lost in, I recommend the ten best adventure games of the 2020s (so far).

The reviews for Asura's Wrath were so scathing that it took me a decade to finally deign to play it, and the sheer shock of finishing it in tears when the credits rolled was beyond words.

Yes, every single one of the comments regarding its poor gameplay was, is, and will be correct, since it's a beat 'em up where the best parts of the gameplay are the on-rails shooting and quick-time events, and that doesn't exactly reflect well on a title of this genre.

Regardless, when you have such an incredible plot, abundant with charismatic characters, memorable scenes, robust mythology, and eccentrically immeasurable cinematics, I couldn't care less that every encounter boils down to mashing the attack button a hundred times a second.

The intercosmic scale that Asura's Wrath handles in its presentation and spectacle is monumental, unique, and emotional enough to overlook its mediocre mechanics, being the only case in the entire genre where it's a masterpiece even without being fun in the traditional sense.

Bucking the trend in the genre, whose disdain for stealth became evident in the last decade, Arkane Studios made a tremendous statement in 2012 with Dishonored's release.

Coming from another underrated gem, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, the studio embraced the lingering force of immersive sims and materialized it into a project that excels as both a stealth game and an action-adventure game.

Boasting some of the best level design in video game history, along with a story that evolves based on the player's actions rather than dialogue choices, Dishonored is one of the century's defining power fantasies.

Between Dunwall's perfect setting, the outstanding array of gadgets and powers that allow for creative and expansive use of stealth and violence, and the majestic musical pieces that accompany us, it's clear that the love for stealth games will never die as long as this IP remains available.

Years go by, and I still wonder if the genre has enough strength to produce a title that surpasses Dishonored, but for now, it remains on the throne without any concern about being replaced.

In this list, we'll discuss our picks for the best action-adventure games that go beyond a hundred hours, from RPGs to known open-world titles.

#4276. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4275. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4273. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4272. Zenless Zone Zero's big end-of-year update brings multiplayer combat, free Zhao, and the first dual-form Agent

Zenless Zone Zero' is saying goodbye to 2025 with a bang, as update 2.5 gets fully revealed.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a big deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s new Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

Zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

There’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. Similar updates are on the way for other Agents, which will arrive in future updates. Shiyu Defense and Deadly Assault has seen some adjustments to the gameplay loop, too.

Finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s new story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire update’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

You’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a new outfit for Jane, and more. #4270. FC 26 adds upgraded Pina alongside 3 new Heroes in full Winter Wildcards promo

Winter Wildcards Team 1 is scarier than Ultimate Scream, featuring buffed Pina, Dembele, Valverde and Rodman cards alongside brand-new Heroes.

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

#4267. Nintendo Indie World Showcase Recap: Everything We Saw

The year is nearing its conclusion, and the last big AAA titles are rolling out one-by-one. But today, it was all about the independent titles on Nintendo's latest Indie World Showcase, highlighting new games from smaller indie teams coming to the Switch and Switch 2.

Here's everything we saw at the October 2026 Nintendo Indie World Showcase.

Today's Indie World Showcase started with a big headliner, as the long-awaited witch-life simulator Witchbrook got a release date. Chucklefish and Robtality's cozy magical world goes live on January 28, 2027.

Fans of 3D platformers should probably keep an eye on Winds of Viridia, which looks like a colorful game with a lot of interesting movement and exploration. Shark Jump's fantastical platformer is arriving next year, but if the wait's too long, a free demo is coming today on the eShop.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The delightfully Game Boy-styled critter delivery game Petal Runner is aiming for a full launch. I've played a bit of this one at events over the years, and it's charmed me every time. If you like nostalgic adventures with a surprisingly heartfelt core, you should mark down the March 8, 2027 launch, or check out the free demo arriving later today.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4266. Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Cast Features A Returning Voice Actor From The N64 Original

Nintendo has today shared even more insights into the development of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 in the latest chapters of its Ask the Developer series. One such story is all about the new voice cast, which apparently features some familiar pipes.

Series Producer Eiji Aonuma and game Director HokWai Ng explain that the team didn't want to "mess with established perceptions of how certain characters sound based on the original," so Nintendo conducted blind auditions to really focus on matching the voice to the role.

"We deliberately hid the voice actors’ names during the Japanese auditions to force ourselves to decide based solely on which voices most closely resembled those of the original," Aonuma-san explains.

As luck would have it, such an approach led Nintendo to select an actor who had previously appeared in the N64 original — voicing the same character, no less! "None of us saw that coming," Aonuma-san notes.

In true Nintendo hush-hush fashion, the interview doesn't mention the voice actor or character by name, but there is already a fair amount of speculation out there that Kaori Mizuhashi (the actor who voiced Navi in the original) might be returning to voice the fairy again this time around.

We won't know for sure until we get to play the game ourselves — and even then, we have to imagine that Mizuhashi would only be handling the Japanese version — but what a neat little bit of luck on Nintendo's part. Hey, you're unlikely to find anyone who sounds more like the N64 original.

The first two chapters of this Ask the Developer series revealed the remake's development team and some design sketches alongside a bunch of other interesting info. You can read more about the highlights in our coverage below.

#4264. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4263. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4262. Nexus Mods Officially Adds AI Disclosures And Preferences

AI has wormed its way into every facet of life. You can't go five minutes without your Gen X parents being duped by the most obvious deepfakes on Facebook; gaming isn't exempt. I could go on a tirade about all the ways in which the industry has buckled under a sewage pipe of generative slop, but the most upsetting impact is that even the collaborative spirit of fan-made mods is being outsourced to machines. Thankfully, the world's biggest mod platform, Nexus, is taking a stand.

"It's no secret that there's been a lot of discussion about AI in the modding community, and in particular our stance on it," site owner Victor 'Foledinho' posted. "The topic is certainly a complex one; we received numerous comments from you guys, and we saw it debated in our Discord channels, comment sections on the site, and even across social media. From the discussions we've had and what we've seen, the issue ranges from the potential use of mods, to avoiding AI-generated content during mod browsing, and seeing AI as a tool that can make modding more accessible. All of those are legitimate concerns worthy of discussion."

Nexus assured that it is "pro-human creativity", but it will not ban AI-generated mods. Instead, it's adopting a similar model to Steam, with mandatory disclosures, including a public explanation of where AI was used, ensuring that players have a more thorough understanding of what they're downloading. However, the team is going a step further than Steam by allowing you to filter out AI mods altogether, with three new content preferences:

"Some of you would prefer not to see any AI-generated content, and that’s your decision to make," Foledinho said. "We’re refining content preference tools so you can enable this control directly from game pages and the homepage, rather than having to find it in the settings. Next up, we'll bring these controls into search and the way mods are displayed on game homepages.

"In addition, we’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," they continued. "This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon."

AI isn't just slop, though. Often, vibecoded projects have worse security or outright hide malicious code. Adding mandatory disclosures will help players to avoid AI-generated mods, and thus less secure mods, but the Nexus team is also investing in security tools and specialized staff specifically to handle Trojans. Already, it has manually reviewed over 3,000 mods, with 20,000 quarantined for further security checks.

"Where we have concerns about safety or a mod’s undisclosed behavior that remain unresolved, we request source code to help us investigate further," Foledinho explained. "Mod Authors are not obliged to provide it, but we may decline to continue hosting it where those concerns cannot be resolved."

Existing mods have two months to implement AI disclosures, and looking ahead, Nexus vows that its policies will continue to evolve alongside AI.

Nexus Mods makes it easier to filter out mods that are made with generative AI, as modders will have to say how AI was used.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4261. Phantom Blade Zero: Here's How To Get The Perfect Ending, Which Is The Only Satisfying One

Phantom Blade Zero is a sprawling Wuxia adventure, the best action game of the year, and one of my favorite action games ever. It offers a lot to do, from main story quests to dozens of side quests, collectibles, hidden bosses, secret areas, and more. I highly recommend checking out Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks before jumping in. It mentions some tasks required to achieve the perfect ending, but here I'll break down exactly what you need to see it.

As a note, getting the perfect ending in Phantom Blade Zero isn't that unreasonable. It requires doing a lot of the game's side content, but it's not shrouded in mystery or puzzles; you just need to complete certain things before heading into the finale. I'm going to keep these requirements relatively spoiler-free, and honestly, without the wider story context, they'll be a lot of mumbo jumbo proper nouns that don't really mean anything. If you're set on getting the perfect ending, I'd bookmark this page, and as you play Phantom Blade Zero, more and more of these requirements will start to make sense. However, if you think even a name or proper noun is a spoiler, be careful reading these requirements.

The following requirements don't necessarily have a set order. You could technically ignore all of this and then go after everything right before the game's "last chance to get things done" warning near the finale. So don't sweat about picking up this or that at a certain time in your journey – do it when you want to. Just make sure you have the following requirements completed before heading past the "last chance" warning.

#4260. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4259. 'The Elder Scrolls 6' Finally Has An Official Title

We forget quite how long we have been waiting for official news from the next entry in Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls series, and now the studio has finally, finally lifted the lid on its title.

As revealed by Todd Howard himself in a new studio 40th anniversary video, the next game in the series is titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel (yep, the very same name that was reported last week).

The reveal doesn't come with much more information than that. There's a brief glimpse of a metallic scroll being unearthed from some sand, the title logo, and the following quote from 'Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell', but that's it:

The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate.

That's all we have right now. Still no release date, still no confirmed platforms, still no gameplay. But hey, a name is a good start!

Given Bethesda's support for Switch 2 so far, our fingers are crossed that we'll see the next series entry come our way at some point (whenever that may be), but there's no official word on that front for the moment, unfortunately.

#4258. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a big game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

#4256. Three Xbox Games Are Shutting Down Their Servers In November & December 2026

A few notable delistings on the way as well

November has officially arrived, and therefore we thought we'd bring you our latest roundup of games getting delisted over the next few weeks, with this roundup specifically focusing on November and December 2026.

The good news is that there's not much to talk about! Call of Duty: Warzone is undoubtedly the most notable of the bunch here, which has been set to go offline on Xbox One and PS4 for some time. They originally announced that it would go offline when Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 began, and that's now officially set for November 6th, 2026.

Beyond that, NBA 2K25 is losing its servers at the end of the year, while Synduality: Echo of Ada is turning off its in-game purchases in December ahead of a planned full server closure in May of 2027.

Beyond this, we also wanted to bring your attention to Amazon's New World: Aeternum, which is officially shutting down its servers at the end of January 2027. We'll remind you again nearer the time, but it's worth being aware of it now too!

As for upcoming delistings, both Street Outlaws and Street Outlaws 2 will disappear off the Xbox Store at the end of December 2026, so you'll need to buy them before then if you want the ability to re-download them in the future.

We've seen on many occasions that announcements like these can spring up at the last minute, so we'll keep an eye out and let you know of any big reveals over the next couple of months. For now though, the damage doesn't look too bad!

#4255. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Remake Review Round-Up

If you were worried about whether The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake could live up to the hype of following in the footsteps of the highest-rated game ever, you can almost certainly put those fears to bed. The reviews for the remake are in, and 2026's Ocarina has almost hit that impossible benchmark set by the original.

The Ocarina remake currently has a 96 on Metacritic and a 95 on OpenCritic. Those scores might jump around a little bit as more reviews are published and their scores accounted for, but it's almost certain that the remake will take the lead for the highest-rated game of the year so far.

It's also about as close as you could hope the game would get to the 99 the original Ocarina scored in 1998. Not only does the N64 game's almost-perfect score make it the highest-rated game of all time, but with fewer reviews published back then, it's a record that will almost certainly never be beaten. If what sounds like a near-perfect remake of the same game can't beat it, then it's difficult to imagine what can.

For comparison, the original Ocarina has 22 published reviews. Its remake already has 48.

As for why those lucky enough to review the remake are giving it such high scores, here at TheGamer, where we awarded the new Ocarina a perfect 5/5, Collin Macgregor writes, "A beautiful, engrossing fantasy adventure that maintains its thrilling combat encounters, clever puzzles, and unique charm. This is the definitive way to experience Ocarina of Time, and know that I envy you if this will be your first time ever playing it."

"The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is a must-play, whether you're a franchise fan or not, and one of the best examples of how to properly reimagine an enduring masterpiece," Destructoid's review reads, in which the remake was also awarded a perfect score. "Ocarina of Time is still a wonder of game design and a thrilling adventure. This remake smooths over some rough edges, leaves others intact, and lets what was so special about the original shine through," writes GameSpot, one of the few outlets not to give Ocarina full marks, awarding it a 9/10.

Although it might not have a perfect score everywhere, pretty much every way you look, when it comes to reviews, people have nothing but the most glowing things to say about how Nintendo handled this remake. Remaking what many consider to be the greatest game of all time was something many feared was unnecessary. Whether you still believe that or not, it sounds like Nintendo has pulled off the impossible and nailed the assignment.

#4254. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4253. Phantom Blade Zero: Longtime Sonic, Ezio Voice Actor Roger Craig Smith Is The New VO For Protagonist Soul

Longtime Sonic the Hedgehog voice actor Roger Craig Smith, who also voices iconic characters such as Ezio Auditore, Chris Redfield, and Batman, is the new voice of Phantom Blade Zero protagonist Soul, according to developer S-Game. Smith replaces former voice actor Jay Maksenuk, who can still be heard voicing Soul in various trailers and gameplay videos.

You can hear Smith's rendition of Soul in the official launch trailer for Phantom Blade Zero, however, below:

Game Informer has reached out to S-Game for a comment or statement on why the VO was changed and will update this story if it learns more.

I can pull back the curtains a bit on how last-minute this change seemingly was for Phantom Blade Zero. For most of my time playing Phantom Blade Zero for review (you can read it here), Soul was still voiced by Maksenuk. I wasn't the biggest fan of the English VO at the time, so I played most of the game using its excellent Chinese VO. However, about a week into the review period for Phantom Blade Zero, developer S-Game told me the VO for Soul had been updated (the team had previously said this update would happen ahead of time).

S-Game didn't say why or who at the time, but after listening to it post-update, it was clear to me it was Smith; his voice is iconic and hard to miss. I was basically at the end of the game at that point, so I didn't get to hear too much, but overall, I like Smith's inclusion as Soul's VO.

Nonetheless, if you're jumping into Phantom Blade Zero at launch, the Soul you play as will be voiced entirely by Smith. Let us know in the comments what you think of it after you've had some time with it!

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review, and then check out these Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks.

#4252. "I Had Some Overdue Homework" - Ocarina Of Time Remake Features More Water Temple Tweaks

Yes, Aonuma knows how much you hate those Iron Boots

It's no secret that Eiji Aonuma can see the issues with Ocarina of Time's Water Temple. The series producer spoke about it when the game launched on 3DS, and it continues to haunt him today, as he's brought it up once again in the latest Ask the Developer interview.

"I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago," Aonuma-san says of the Switch 2 remake. He touches on all the dungeon's much-discussed sticking points (the item menu annoyances, confusing layout, etc.), and confirms that he "had the team make some adjustments in this version".

Director HokWai Ng expands on these changes, stating that the Switch 2 remake has "made item toggling much easier" — it's now mapped to the D-pad, borrowing from the simplicity of the 3DS version — and there have been certain structural tweaks, too: "We also changed some of the walls that made it easy to lose your sense of direction to lattice-style structures, making it possible to see the rooms beyond them and get a better sense of the overall space."

What's interesting is seeing Aonuma-san speak about his intentions behind the dungeon's original design. It always gets so bogged down in negativity that it's nice to get a reminder about where it all came from:

When I designed the Water Temple all those years ago, I wanted to create an experience where simply being underwater was fun. It was a time when there were very few 3D games that even let players go underwater. I enjoy freediving, and what I find fascinating about being underwater is how different everything feels. The sounds change, and it feels like you’re in a completely different space. I wanted to create a place where players could experience those sensations.

Of course, the 3DS version came with its own Water Temple tweaks, including mapping the Iron Boots toggle to the touchscreen and adding directional lines leading to the water level switches on all the walls.

And yet, there are still those of us on Team NL that love the Water Temple in its original form — warts and all. It'll be interesting to see how the Switch 2 version matches up later this week.

#4251. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4250. Fortnite Datamine Reveals Finishers With Custom Animations

Fortnite is no stranger to lifting ideas from other games and incorporating them into its hugely successful battle royale. It looks like the next example of that might be finishing moves, perhaps functioning in a similar way to the ones you can perform in Call of Duty.

According to Hypex, but originally discovered and shared by a10tion and Nova, Epic Games is working on a finishing move mechanic that will let you eliminate knocked opponents in style. So not exactly like sneaking up behind an opponent for an execution like in Call of Duty, but a similar premise that appears to have been inspired by it.

The datamined details about Fortnite finishers reveal that, when performed on a downed opponent, you and the targeted player will cut to a custom animation. Again, similar to Call of Duty, although there are countless games where that’s the case, dating all the way back to the iconic finishers in the original Mortal Kombat games.

There will be multiple animations, which potentially sounds like these are essentially going to be cosmetic items that can be unlocked, giving players the chance to try and obtain rarer finishers than anyone else, similar to everything else you can unlock in Fortnite. Think of them as emotes, except rather than picking and choosing when you perform them, the animations will only ever be activated when you’re adding insult to injury by eliminating a knocked player from the match.

The only other information gleaned from the finishing moves datamine for now is that there will be quests attached to the new mechanic. Presumably just quests that task you with performing finishing moves on a certain number of opponents to earn, what I would hope, will be a significant amount of XP. As much as I’m eager to start performing finishers in Fortnite, it’s going to be tricky, particularly on a busy map, as you’ll be a sitting duck should anyone spot you while that custom animation is doing its thing.

Finishing moves will provide another way for Fortnite to embed other IPs into its big, mixed-up universe. Mortal Kombat’s Scorpion is already in the game, so adding a “Get over here” finishing move would make all the sense in the world. I’m also now all-encompassed by the idea of using Seth Rollins’ Curb Stomp on someone to score a victory royale. If that move is ever added to Fortnite, I will play nothing else until I make that dream a reality. I don’t care if it takes me years.
